items.text: Land, factories and other major productive assets should be owned in common, by those who work them or by the whole community.
items.note: Productive assets: things used to make goods or provide services, such as land, factories, machines and companies.
items.rationale: Core socialist/communist/anarcho-communist claim, phrased without a state actor; ideal vs here-and-now can split for gradualists.

items.text: Large businesses should be owned by the people who work in them.
items.rationale: Co-operativists, market socialists and syndicalists endorse; works as a standing rule in any system or country.

items.text: If only one provider can supply an essential service such as water or power, that provider should be owned by the public or its users.
items.rationale: Natural-monopoly condition favours Collective; social democrats and municipalists endorse; plausible frame split where privatised utilities exist.

items.text: If the owners of a profitable workplace decide to close it, its workers should be able to take it over as their own.
items.rationale: Worker-recovered-enterprise view (syndicalist, autonomist, left-populist); strong because it overrides owners' title; meaningful in both frames.

items.text: Wealth should be spread roughly evenly across a society.
items.rationale: Egalitarians (socialist, social-democratic, some religious-communitarian) endorse; outcome phrasing so anarchists can answer.

items.text: If a few people end up owning most of the wealth, some of it should be shared out among everyone else.
items.rationale: Concentration condition favours Collective; moderate redistributionists across left and populist-right endorse; condition assumed true in each frame.

items.text: Wealth should be distributed according to each person's needs.
items.rationale: Communist and anarcho-communist distributive principle (from each/to each); strong pole; ideal-minded respondents may answer differently here and now.

items.text: Nearly all land and productive assets should be owned privately, by individuals or the businesses they form.
items.note: Productive assets: things used to make goods or provide services, such as land, factories, machines and companies.
items.rationale: Mirror of col-01; classical liberals, libertarians and anarcho-capitalists endorse; strong pole, agent-neutral.

items.text: Most businesses should be owned by private individuals, families or investors.
items.rationale: Mainstream conservative, liberal and Christian-democratic view; mirror of col-02; reads as a standing rule in both frames.

items.text: If a publicly or commonly owned enterprise keeps running at a loss, it should be sold to private owners.
items.rationale: Failure condition favours Private (mirror of col-03); market liberals and fiscal conservatives endorse; likely frame split where loss-making public firms exist.

items.text: If someone builds a business from nothing, they should keep full ownership of it, however large it grows.
items.rationale: Founder/entitlement view (libertarian, Lockean, propertarian) favours Private; strong because it rules out any size-based claim; mirror of col-04.

items.text: Large gaps in wealth should be accepted when they come from work, skill or fair trade.
items.rationale: Meritocratic liberals and conservatives endorse; mirror of col-05; answerable in both frames without naming an agent.

items.text: If people grow rich by selling things others freely choose to buy, they should be able to keep most of that wealth.
items.rationale: Voluntary-exchange condition favours Private (mirror of col-06); market liberals endorse; 'most' keeps it at a clear rather than absolute lean.

items.text: Wealth should belong wholly to whoever earned it or was freely given it, whatever other people's needs.
items.rationale: Nozickian entitlement view held by libertarians and anarcho-capitalists; direct strong mirror of col-07's needs principle.
